newsitem.title: GERMANY: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 4.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 4.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

BERLIN - Top German television groups ProSieben Media AG and the RTL network say they will raise advertising prices in 1998. ProSieben will raise ad prices an average of 4.6 percent while RTL, Germany's largest station, will increase prices an average 5.5 percent.

LONDON - Britain's television watchdog says it upheld complaints against three different car commercials and warns that car ads must not condone irresponsible driving. The Independent Television Commission says it upheld complaints against BMP DDB Needham's ads for the Volkswagen Passat and Volkswagen Polo and Ogilvy & Mather's ad for the Ford Fiesta.

DALLAS - Targeting leisure travellers to fuel continued growth, America West Airlines puts its estimated $37 million-plus advertising account in review. The Phoenix-based carrier has invited two-year incumbent agency Team One, Los Angeles, to participate, says a spokeswoman, and the airline plans to hire an outside consultant to assist with the review, which could take as long as six months to complete.

VIENNA - Fast-food chain McDonalds Austria is in a pickle over its latest advertising gimmick, which has placemats featuring a map of the country as devised by Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler. McDonalds told Die Kurier daily that it had simply wanted to highlight the beef-producing regions of Austria on the paper mats which cover its trays.

RENO, Nevada - U.S. beef producers devise a brand-identity marketing campaign that it hopes will stem a decade-long slide in beef sales. The National Cattlement's Beef Association will launch a pilot campaign in 1998, using a new beef symbol that will appear on beef products judged to be consistent in quality and taste.

LONDON - International Poster Management, a unit of Interpublic Group of Cos Inc, says it acquired a majority stake in Business Geographics Ltd, which uses geo-demographic data to target media, marketing and business development toward specific consumer groups.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LONDON - British Telecommunications Plc is expected to announce an alliance with Japan's Fujitsu Ltd and France's Alcatel that could revolutionise the telephone network, the Sunday Telegraph says. The venture would allow BT to carry video and Internet sercies on enhance telephone lines, and the link-up with the two companies is expected to be announced later this month.

SEATTLE - Microsoft Corp. says it completed the acquisition of WebTV Networks Inc. for about $425 million in cash and stock hours after the U.S. Department of Justice announced its approval of the deal. Steve Perlman, co-founder of the company, which offers Internet service through television set-top boxes, retains his title as chief executive officer.

PARIS - French broadcasting regulator Conseil Superieur de l'audiovisuel (CSA) says Lagardere Group's radio stations cover a population bigger than that allowed by law since the regrouping of its interests in Hachette Filipacchi Medias. Lagardere, which contests this, may have to sell RFM or Skyrock.
LONDON - The BBC says it has reached an agreement with Jordan Radio and Television to make radio broadcasts on 24-hour FM frequency in Amman.

PARIS - Private television channel M6 says it was justified in refusing to carry adverts promoting pay television station Canal Plus because Canal Plus's hours of uncoded broadcasting compete directly with M6 both for advertising and programming.

LONDON - The Daily Mail and General Trust Plc say losses in the current year at its Channel One cable television subsidiary will be similar to 1996 levels, but it expects losses at Channel One will fall "significantly" next year as a result of a lower cost base and more targeted programming.

LONDON - Pearson Chief Executive Marjorie Scardino vows to double the value of the company and unveils better-than-expected first-half figures as a "first step" on the road to improved performance. Pearson, owner of prized assets such as the Financial Times newspaper and Penguin books, said profit from continuing operations almost doubled to 65.5 million pounds in the first six months of 1997.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

ABIDJAN - The Marlboro Cowboy may be riding into the sunset in rich countries with anti-smoking campaigners snapping at his heels. But in Africa, with its vast horizon and young and rapidly expanding population, there is no sign that anyone is looking to run him out of town any time soon. Cigarette companies are scrambling to Africa's emerging markets from South Africa to Ivory Coast.

TOKYO - Japanese auto giant Toyota Motor Corp says it hopes to grab a slice of the promising Indian auto market through a joint venture to produce and sell multi-purpose vehicles for large Indian families. The joint venture with firms in the Kirloskar Group, India's leading engineering group, will have a total investment of $170 million.
LONDON - British pub operator J.D. Wetherspoon Plc says it has banned the sale of 'alcopops' - alcoholic lemonades and sodas - from its pubs following the controversy about the drinks.

WALLDORF - German software group SAP AG and computer chip maker Intel Corp plan to announce an Internet commerce joint venture on August 5, SAP says. The venture's goal is to develop a software product that supports business applications on the Internet, says SAP.

PARIS - Car sales in France fell 9.7 percent in July, the seventh consecutive monthly fall from inflated 1996 levels, but Renault sales advanced against the trend, the French carmakers' committee CCFA says. Car industry analysts are beginning to discern a rebound in the French automotive sector following a 20 percent fall this year in sales.

ADELAIDE - Australian winemakers say looming drought conditions may cut back expected tonnages for the 1998 vintage, but they believe lessons learnt from the disastrous 1994-95 drought should mitigate losses. Australia's biggest winemaker, Southcorp Wines, a division of Southcorp Holdings Ltd, says drought conditions could affect up to 20 percent of its vineyards.

DETROIT - General Motors Corp. posts an unexpected 6 percent jump in U.S. sales for July, but Toyota and Honda continue to outperform their American rivals. Sales at Chrysler Corp. fall 9 percent in July.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LONDON - Half a century may have passed since the sun set on British rule in India, but curry remains as popular as ever in Britain, according to a survey. An astonishing 205 million poppadoms -- along with 111 million pints of beer -- are consumed in Indian restaurants in Britain each year, the report says. There are more Indian restaurants in Greater London than in Bombay and New Delhi combined.
LONDON - Sales of personal computers in western Europe gathered pace in the first half of 1997 and are likely to accelerate in the second half, says a report by market researcher CONTEXT.

LONDON - Europe's market for organic food is booming. Consumer interest is increasing and demand far outstrips supply, say government officials and analysts of the food retail business. The market in Britain for organic food -- although still modest -- has expanded dramatically, by around 20 percent a year since the mid-1980s, with demand jumping in reaction to various food scares.
